source_evidence.observation: A random variable has symmetric Bernoulli, also called Rademacher, distribution exactly when it takes the values −1 and 1 with probability 1/2 each.
The source defines the sub-gaussian norm by ‖X‖ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2} and calls a random variable satisfying the equivalent properties i–iv of Proposition 2.5.2 sub-gaussian.
For a symmetric Bernoulli random variable X, the source states |X| = 1 and concludes that X is sub-gaussian.
The source gives the exact equality ‖X‖ψ₂ = 1/√(ln 2).

hypotheses: X has symmetric Bernoulli, equivalently Rademacher, distribution: P{X = −1} = P{X = 1} = 1/2.
conclusions: X is a sub-gaussian random variable.
definitions_and_conventions: Symmetric Bernoulli, or Rademacher, distribution means that the only values are −1 and 1, each with probability 1/2.
The sub-gaussian norm is ‖X‖ψ₂ = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
Because a symmetric Bernoulli variable satisfies |X| = 1, one has X² = 1 almost surely.
The notation ln denotes the natural logarithm.
implicit_context: X is defined on an underlying probability space, and P and E denote probability and expectation on that space.
No independence, auxiliary random variables, centering hypothesis, or additional parameter is part of this one-variable example.
The exact norm value uses the threshold 2 fixed by Definition 2.5.6.

details: The distribution is symmetric on the two points −1 and 1.
The term Bernoulli in this example means symmetric Bernoulli/Rademacher, not a {0,1}-valued Bernoulli variable.
Sub-gaussianity is governed by Definition 2.5.6 and its exponential-square integrability condition.
The admissible scales are real t > 0 and the expectation threshold is exactly 2.
Since X² = 1 almost surely, E exp(X²/t²) = exp(1/t²).
The threshold exp(1/t²) ≤ 2 begins at t = 1/√(ln 2), yielding the displayed infimum exactly.
The source asserts equality, not merely an upper or lower bound.
The constant is exactly 1/√(ln 2), not an unspecified absolute constant.

undebatable_constraints: X must have the symmetric Bernoulli/Rademacher distribution with values −1 and 1 and probability 1/2 at each value.
The conclusion must include that X is sub-gaussian.
The ψ₂ norm must retain the source definition inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The norm conclusion must be the exact equality ‖X‖ψ₂ = 1/√(ln 2), not only an inequality.
No independence, sequence, mean-zero premise, or additional distributional hypothesis may be added.
contracts.contract_plain_english: If X is a Rademacher random variable—equal to −1 and 1 with probability 1/2 each—then X is sub-gaussian, and under the source's threshold-2 definition its ψ₂ norm is exactly 1/√(ln 2).
